Dotted: AUC 0.5; dashed: 0.60 triage line. figD4_paired_differences: Paired differences on the same patients and splits, pretrained DynaMix minus each comparator (three separate random initializations, and saved E01c). Left/middle: mean-over-repeats AUC difference with joint patient-bootstrap interval. Right: patient-level paired difference in log-loss averaged over the three repeats (each patient contributes one number), Remitter. Intervals are conditional on saved predictions. A difference to a random model addresses whether pretraining changes these features, not whether the features predict; a difference to E01c is descriptive, not a superiority test.
figD5_roc_pr: Remitter, pooled out-of-fold predictions. Thick = repeat 42 (prespecified primary), thin = repeats 43/44 (not selected). Left: ROC. Right: precision-recall; dotted = prevalence (0.48). Descriptive curves only; thresholds were fixed inside training folds and are not chosen from these curves. Curves near the diagonal/prevalence line indicate no useful ranking.
figD6_calibration: Remitter calibration (reliability) of pooled out-of-fold probabilities in five equal-count bins (thick = repeat 42, thin = 43/44; n per bin shown for 42). Points near the dotted diagonal would indicate calibrated probabilities; with ~33 patients per bin the observed fractions carry roughly +/-0.09 binomial noise.
figD7_representation_stability: Label-free diagnostics of the DynaMix summaries (one dot = one of the 12 feature types, median over 26 channels; recordings with >=2 eligible windows pooled over EC and EO per model; no outcome data). Left: whether a patient's first-window summary predicts the later windows. Middle: how much variance lies between recordings versus across windows of the same recording. Right: numerical stability to gating noise. These speak to representation stability only; stable features are not necessarily predictive, and amplitude information is discarded by the per-series standardization.
